text: WASHINGTON — Calling Donald Trump merely a bad president doesn't go far enough. Even "King" is too good a word for the likes of him. In the end, what Trump truly is shall be written. Until now, Andrew Johnson was the worst president we've had. Johnson, a Southerner and Abraham Lincoln's vice president, assumed office in 1865 after the Civil War president was murdered by a Confederate sympathizer.

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Public leadership doesn't mean that the "leader" has to have all the solutions, but instead must be open to others with problem-solving ideas. That was one of Franklin Roosevelt's great strengths when he came into the White House. Facing the full-blown crisis of a national depression, he brought his top advisers together with an open mandate for creativity: "Do something," he told them. "If it works, do more of it. If it doesn't work, do something else."

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: A public "leader" need not possess every solution. What public leadership requires instead is openness to other people's ideas for solving problems. Franklin Roosevelt demonstrated that strength when he entered the White House amid the full-blown crisis of a national depression. He gathered his top advisers and gave them an open mandate to be creative: "Do something," he told them. "If it works, do more of it. If it doesn't work, do something else."

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: There's an old saying: Those who can, do; those who can't, teach. A similar idea underscores the debate over wealth taxes in California and elsewhere: Those who can, build companies. Those who can't, devise ways for the government to take shares in what others have built.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Classic Labor Day imagery shows men wearing hard hats and tough women in uniforms. These are Americans who did not build their muscles at a wellness club. By contrast, actual photos of the Democratic Socialists of America show seas of white faces belonging to college graduates. The only work most of them have done with their hands is typing. But the DSA is run by leaders who pretend otherwise, pushing forward candidates who play-act as tradespeople.

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing

label: Right-wing
text: President Trump's new chair of the Council of Economic Advisers, Kevin Hassett, walked into the lion's den last week with his first official speech. He used the moment to pound the leftist Tax Policy Center. It was a wonderful sight.

author: veronique-de-rugy
label: Right-wing
text: Most Americans apparently agree on at least one thing. Unfortunately, it's something dangerous: price controls. A new Wall Street Journal poll finds remarkable bipartisan support for government limits on prices, with 93% of Democrats and 83% of Republicans supporting capping prescription drug prices. Nearly four in five voters support capping credit card interest rates at 10%. And large majorities favor capping child care charges for working families.

label: Left-wing

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing
text: Growing up, I received a wealth of working-class values from my parents, including this nugget about egalitarianism: "Nobody is better than you," they said, "and you're no better than anybody else." That's the ethical underpinning for "We're all in this together" — it's what Thomas Jefferson enshrined in the Declaration of Independence and it's what Lincoln consecrated in his Gettysburg address; it's in our own pledge of allegiance to "liberty and justice for all;" it's what the Statue of Liberty welcomes; it's Woody Guthrie's anthem to the Common Good; and ... well, it's AMERICA!

author: jim-hightower
label: Left-wing

author: froma-harrop
label: Right-wing
text: Brides should know that they already have a man. They don't have to use their wedding to attract a date for Saturday night. They've supposedly secured one for the foreseeable future. author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing
text: WASHINGTON — Camelot, it's not. King Arthur, not even close. Donald Trump is a pretender president who doesn't even pretend to do right by the people. In all candor, this city, graced by garden squares, memorials and museums, feels like a crime scene, with his fingerprints everywhere on it. Places we held dear are demolished (the White House East Wing) or closed (the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts). But who knows what's in the knave's heart?

author: jamie-stiehm
label: Left-wing

In all candor, with his fingerprints everywhere, this city of garden squares, memorials and museums feels like a crime scene. The White House East Wing, one of the places we held dear, has been demolished; another, the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, is closed. Yet who can know what's in the knave's heart?

text: One of the most unheralded policy successes of President Donald Trump's second term has been the purging of many unnecessary federal jobs. Not since President Lyndon Johnson's Great Society vastly expanded the scope of the national government has the federal workforce been at this level.

label: Left-wing
text: Executives climbing the corporate ladder to the top seem to lose IQ the higher up they get.
